report:
Summary finding
- The difference between the checkpoints is not a hidden "capability" change but a systematic shift in the model's prior at the start of a sequence: Model B (B − A positive) changes the residual-stream activations overwhelmingly at token-position 0 across many layers, producing a different first-token bias. I cannot identify a specific training objective from this evidence, but the data strongly supports a change in the initial-token/logit prior rather than a localized downstream behaviour.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial concentration: the L2-norm table shows the vast majority of the activation difference concentrated at position 0 (p0) across layers, growing with depth and peaking in late layers (layers ~20–25). Pos1–pos4 are much smaller by comparison. That pattern means the models differ mainly in how they set up the residual stream for the first token (the unconditional / start-of-sequence prior).
- Logit-lens content: the top-vocabulary directions for the high-norm (mainly pos0) cells show consistent, interpretable shifts in the kinds of words those difference vectors point to. Early-layer pos0 directions include tokens like "bottle", "Baja", "wings"; mid/late-layer pos0 directions include "Stay", "Every", "Do", "rejected", "normal", "human", "relevant", and then later a cluster of words with negative/urgent/event connotations: "tragic", "tragedy", "law", "surgeon", "clinic", "downturn", "rescue", "shocked", "blitz", "coming", "forced", etc. This indicates the difference changes which initial tokens (and thus which kinds of continuations) are favored.
- Coherence of effect: the tokens pointed at by many high-norm pos0 cells form a non-random pattern (imperative/advice words and words about incidents/tragedy/medical/law), consistent with a semantic shift in the BOS prior rather than pure numerical noise.

What I cannot (responsibly) claim
- I cannot name a precise training objective or dataset that caused this change. The evidence supports "a changed first-token prior / start-of-sequence bias" but does not uniquely identify why (e.g., a specific fine-tune on news, safety, moderation, or stylistic data).
- I also cannot definitively say how this manifests in long continuations because the patchscope continuations were not shown here; however, given the magnitude and lexical pattern of the pos0 changes, one should expect systematic differences in the first word(s) and hence the topic/style of continuations.

Short practical description
- Model B differs from Model A mainly in its initial-token (BOS) residual; B will, on average, prefer a different set of first tokens (and hence different starting topics/tone) than A.
